Both teams entered the arena with high stakes on the line, delivering a match filled with tactical intrigue and individual brilliance. A Lightning Start at the Luz The match ignited almost immediately, with the home side finding their rhythm in the opening moments. In just the 2nd minute, Rafa Silva showcased his clinical edge, slotting the ball home with his right foot to give Benfica an early lead. The early goal set a frantic pace, leading to some heavy challenges. Leandro Barreiro received a yellow card in the 9th minute, followed by Tomas Araujo in the 24th minute after a tactical foul stopped a dangerous counter-attack. Benfica 's persistence paid off again in the 31st minute when Clement Lenglet 's vision allowed Leandro Barreiro to pounce on a loose ball. Barreiro finished with his left foot to double the advantage. However, Aarhus refused to back down. Vangelis Pavlidis stepped up to the spot and calmly sent goalkeeper Mads Hedenstad Christiansen the wrong way with a right-footed shot, ensuring the Eagles went into the break with a significant cushion. Tactical Discipline and Closing Out The second half saw both managers turn to their benches to influence the flow. Aarhus introduced Stefen Tchamche and Rasmus Carstensen early on to find an equalizer, while Benfica responded by bringing on Jhon Duran and Andreas Schjelderup to maintain their offensive threat. The game became a battle of wits in the midfield, with fewer clear-cut chances than the opening period. As the clock ticked down, Stefen Tchamche saw yellow for a rough foul in the 83rd minute, symbolizing the frustration of the visitors. Benfica navigated the final stages professionally, introducing Fredrik Aursnes and Jakub Kaminski to solidify the midfield. After five minutes of stoppage time, the referee blew the final whistle, confirming a vital victory for Benfica in their European campaign.

FC Midtjylland found themselves under pressure early on, leading to a yellow card for Mads Bech in the 35th minute following a handball. The situation grew more precarious for the hosts just before the interval when Martin Erlic was booked for a dangerous challenge. Despite the tension, the teams headed into the break with the deadlock unbroken, though the disciplinary tightrope was becoming a major concern for the Danish side. Red Card Reshapes the Contest The match reached a turning point in the 53rd minute when Martin Erlic received his second yellow card and was sent off. The visitors' patience was rewarded in the 70th minute when substitute Milot Rashica clinical finish found the back of the net after a clever assist from Junior Olaitan . Building on their lead, the Turkish giants doubled their advantage just six minutes later. A penalty was awarded following a foul by Rasmus Nissen , and Orkun Kokcu stepped up to power the ball past Elias Olafsson from the spot. Late frustrations saw Vincenzo Italiano booked for dissent, but Besiktas remained professional, controlling the tempo until the final whistle to secure a well-earned victory on the road.
